answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a small refundable stake that is slashed when its work is proven fake, so creating thousands of fake agents costs real money instead of just compute. Like a ripple spreading through water, the stake is verified by many independent peers before the agent is trusted, and each verified action adds a pulse of reputation history that a fresh fake cannot imitate. An opal-like record, hard to fake and easy to check, makes the attacker cost grow with every identity while honest agents pay almost nothing.
